site.name: lumen-research
site.summary: Lumen Research — research assistant (local demo) Fictional research-assistant chat product. Local fixture for UXBench. Open `index.html` directly. Page `index.html` — Research thread Three-column layout: left rail for thread history, center conversation, right rail for Sources. Center column: - Conversation styled with serif body type. Each assistant turn renders inline citations as small chips (`[1]`, `[2]` …). Hovering a citation highlights and scrolls the matching source on the right; clicking jumps to it. - Embedded tables and lists are styled with the rest of the conversation.

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full lumen-research system, prioritizing the primary chatbot/agent interface flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The Lumen Research chatbot interface has several UX issues. Thread switching often fails to update the conversation and sources rails. Citation chip interactions (hover/click) frequently time out, hindering source navigation. The 'Export as PDF' button and '+ New thread' button lack visible feedback. Mobile viewports have horizontal overflow and small tap targets, reducing usability. Many follow-up buttons and filters remain untested, limiting confidence in full functionality.

exploration_plan.goal: Explore and critique the UX of the Lumen Research chatbot interface, focusing on the primary research-assistant flow, thread navigation, citation interactions, and mobile responsiveness.
exploration_plan.summary: The exploration will proceed in phases: first, validate the main chat interaction and citation functionality on desktop. Then, test thread navigation and export features. Next, check mobile responsiveness and re-verify key interactions. Finally, explore secondary threads and edge cases like new thread creation and mode switching.
assumptions: The site has only one HTML page (index.html) with a multi-thread chat interface.
Citation chips ([1], [2], etc.) link to sources in the right rail.
Thread navigation is via the left rail links.
risk_hotspots: Citation chip interactions (hover/click) for source navigation
Small tap targets on mobile (left rail links)

phases.title: Main Chat Interaction & Citations
phases.objective: Validate the core chat experience and citation linking.
key_checks: Click a citation chip (e.g., [1], [2]) to verify it jumps to the correct source in the right rail.
Hover a citation chip to check if it highlights the matching source (scroll behavior).
Interact with the text input field (ask a follow-up) and submit a query (using the 'Ask' button).
exit_criteria: Citation linking (click/hover) works, and text input/submit is functional.

phases.title: Thread Navigation & Export
phases.objective: Test thread switching and export/share features.
key_checks: Click a different thread in the left rail (e.g., 'EV battery recycling policy in Norway') to switch conversations.
Click 'Export as PDF' to verify the export functionality (check for download or confirmation).
Click 'Share thread' to test the sharing feature (check for modal or link generation).
exit_criteria: Thread switching works, and export/share features are responsive.

phases.title: Mobile Responsiveness (Desktop → Mobile)
phases.objective: Validate the interface on mobile viewport, focusing on tap targets and layout.
key_checks: Switch to mobile viewport and recheck citation chip interactions (click/hover).
Test thread navigation on mobile (tap left rail links) — check for small tap target issues (per layout warnings).
Verify text input and button sizes on mobile (ensure they're touch-friendly).
exit_criteria: Key interactions work on mobile, and tap targets are usable (or issues are documented).

phases.title: Mode Switching & Secondary Threads
phases.objective: Explore mode dropdowns and secondary thread workflows.
key_checks: Interact with the mode dropdown (e.g., 'Balanced' → 'Quick scan') to switch modes and check UI updates.
Click '+ New thread' to create a new conversation and verify thread creation flow.
Switch back to the original thread ('Deep work scheduling literature') to confirm thread management.
exit_criteria: Mode switching updates the UI, and new thread creation/management works.

phases.title: Edge Cases & Accessibility Checks
phases.objective: Test edge cases and accessibility-related elements (unlabeled selects, small targets).
key_checks: Interact with unlabeled select elements (e.g., mode dropdowns) to check for usability (aria-labels or tooltips).
Check the 'Sort: Relevance' dropdown in the sources rail to verify sorting options.
Test the 'New thread' button on mobile to check tap target size (per layout warnings).
exit_criteria: Unlabeled selects are usable (or issues are documented), and sorting works.

coverage_targets.pages: Visit and interact with all known pages (only index.html, so fully explore it).
coverage_targets.features: Exercise all visible controls: text input, citation chips, thread links, export/share, mode dropdowns, source sorting, and new thread creation.
coverage_targets.mobile: Repeat critical checks (citation links, thread navigation, text input) on mobile viewport.

notes: Since there's only one HTML page, focus on different states and interactions within index.html. Document any layout warnings (small tap targets, unlabeled selects) as part of the critique.

findings.user_goal: Switch between chat threads to view different conversations and sources
findings.problem: Clicking on different threads in the left rail (e.g., 'EV battery recycling policy in Norway', 'Trace prevalence of seal influenza H10N7') does not update the center conversation or right sources rails, leaving the UI unchanged.
findings.evidence: Multiple thread click actions (e.g., steps 6, 8, 9) resulted in no visible UI updates. The center column still showed 'Deep work scheduling literature' content after clicking other threads.
findings.why_it_matters: Users cannot navigate between different research threads, preventing access to relevant conversations and sources for their tasks.
findings.suggestion: Fix the thread switching logic to ensure the center and right rails update dynamically when a thread is selected. Add loading indicators or visual feedback during thread transitions.

findings.user_goal: Interact with citation chips to view related sources
findings.problem: Hover and click actions on citation chips (e.g., [1], [2]) frequently time out, failing to highlight or navigate to the corresponding source in the right rail.
findings.evidence: Hover (steps 1, 7) and click (steps 2, 3, 7) actions on citation chips resulted in timeouts. The locator for 'data-uxagent-id="1"' could not be found within the timeout period, despite the chip being visible.
findings.why_it_matters: Users cannot access or verify the sources cited in the chatbot's responses, reducing the credibility and usability of the research assistant.
findings.suggestion: Improve the element identification and interactability of citation chips. Ensure hover highlights and click navigation to sources work reliably. Add error handling for failed interactions.

findings.user_goal: Export the chat conversation as a PDF
findings.problem: Clicking the 'Export as PDF' button does not trigger a download prompt, confirmation message, or any visible UI change.
findings.evidence: Step 5: Clicking 'Export as PDF' (target_id: ux-13) resulted in no URL change, download prompt, or visible feedback. The page remained unchanged.
findings.why_it_matters: Users cannot confirm if the export action was successful, leading to confusion about whether their conversation was exported.
findings.suggestion: Add visible feedback (e.g., a download prompt, confirmation message, or loading indicator) when the 'Export as PDF' button is clicked. Ensure the export functionality works as intended.

findings.user_goal: Use the chatbot interface on a mobile device
findings.problem: The mobile viewport has horizontal overflow (page width 515px > viewport 390px) and small tap targets (e.g., '📎' button 32x35px, 'Ask' button 60x39px) below mobile accessibility guidelines (44px minimum).
findings.evidence: Layout warnings in mobile viewports (e.g., step 31, final observation) show horizontal overflow and small tap targets. The '📎' button (32x35px) and 'Ask' button (60x39px) are below 44px height/width recommendations.
findings.why_it_matters: Mobile users experience difficulty navigating and interacting with the interface due to overflow (requiring horizontal scrolling) and hard-to-tap elements, reducing accessibility and usability.
findings.suggestion: Optimize the mobile layout to eliminate horizontal overflow. Increase the size of tap targets (e.g., buttons, citation chips) to at least 44x44px for better mobile interaction.

findings.problem: Clicking the '+ New thread' button does not create a new thread or update the UI (e.g., no new thread in the left rail, conversation area unchanged).
findings.evidence: Step 31: Clicking '+ New thread' resulted in no visible UI updates. The left rail still showed the existing threads, and the conversation area remained the same.
findings.why_it_matters: Users cannot initiate new research threads, limiting the ability to start fresh conversations or organize research topics.
findings.suggestion: Fix the 'New thread' functionality to create a new thread and update the UI. Add visual feedback (e.g., a new thread in the left rail, empty conversation area) when the button is clicked.

findings.user_goal: Interact with follow-up buttons to get more information
findings.problem: Many follow-up buttons (e.g., 'Find papers since 2020...', 'Power analysis...') do not trigger visible responses or updates, leaving the UI unchanged.
findings.evidence: Steps 19, 20, 21: Clicking follow-up buttons like 'Find papers since 2020 directly comparing the two schedules' and 'Power analysis for 24 engineers × 2 weeks' resulted in no visible text or URL changes.
findings.why_it_matters: Users cannot access additional research or follow-up information, limiting the chatbot's ability to provide in-depth support for their queries.
findings.suggestion: Ensure follow-up buttons trigger the chatbot to generate responses or update the conversation. Add loading indicators or feedback to show the action is processing.

findings.user_goal: Interact with form fields and dropdowns
findings.problem: Multiple form fields (e.g., mode dropdown, sources filter dropdown) lack visible labels, aria-labels, or placeholders, reducing accessibility for screen reader users.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings (e.g., step 31) identify form fields (target_ids: ux-3, ux-6) with no labels. The mode dropdown and sources filter dropdown have no visible labels.
findings.why_it_matters: Screen reader users cannot easily identify or interact with form fields, violating accessibility standards and reducing usability for visually impaired users.
findings.suggestion: Add visible labels, aria-labels, or placeholders to all form fields (e.g., dropdowns, input fields) to improve accessibility.

gaps: 8 browser action(s) failed and should be retried or analyzed.
52% of actions produced no visible URL/text change; this may indicate dead controls or repeated probes.
